_what: SSOT for NON-Claude agent backends — the provider half of the /accounts question. Deployed as a symlink at ~/.claude/providers.json (install.sh), read by bin/claude-accounts to render an ADDITIVE provider section. Deliberately a separate file from accounts.json: that file declares itself SSOT for the 4 Claude Max accounts and every field in it is Anthropic-specific (keychain_account, oauth_client_id, usage_endpoint, token_endpoint). Grafting providers in there would have made its own _what false.
_why_this_exists: /accounts could answer 'which of my 4 Claude Max accounts has headroom' but not 'what agent capacity do I have across all my plans', which is the question that actually governs routing once more than one vendor's plan is held. See docs/plans/MULTI_PROVIDER_PLANS.md.
_the_detection_rule: 🚨 ROUTABILITY IS NOT PRESENCE. Three facts are independent: (1) a binary is on PATH, (2) it is authenticated, (3) it has a NON-INTERACTIVE agent mode. Only (3) decides whether this fleet can route work to it, and it is the one a naive detector skips. Measured 2026-08-10: grok-wiki's picker reported Antigravity `ready` on the strength of `command -v antigravity` alone — but that binary is the VS Code editor launcher (its --help is byte-for-byte VS Code's: --install-extension, --user-data-dir, --add-mcp) and has NO exec/agent/headless subcommand at all. It can never be routed to, whatever its auth says. Hence `headless` below: a provider with headless:null is NOT a backend and renders as such, however healthy it looks.
_the_cost_rule: 🚨 ASK WHAT IT BILLS, NOT WHAT IT CAN LOG INTO. `bills_outside_plan` is the gate, and it is a DIFFERENT question from `plan`. Measured 2026-08-10: Pi's README lists 'Anthropic Claude Pro/Max' under Subscriptions — true about authentication, silent about billing — while the same package's docs/providers.md states third-party harness usage 'draws from extra usage and is billed per token, not against Claude plan limits'. A subscription LOGIN LIST answers only whether auth works; it will never volunteer the meter. Any provider whose answer here is true, or UNKNOWN, is documented and SKIPPED — never wired, never signed up for. Cross-check against accounts.json spend.usage_credits_authorized before ever flipping one to false.
_provenance: Every row was established from a live read on 2026-08-10 and carries the command in `established_by`. A field that could not be measured is null and renders UNKNOWN — never a guess.

_stale_catalog_rule: 🚨 UPDATE THE CLI BEFORE READING ITS MODEL LIST. A model catalog cached on disk can simultaneously hide newer models AND be unreadable by an older client. Measured 2026-08-10: ~/.codex/models_cache.json was stamped client_version 0.142.2 and listed 5 models — omitting gpt-5.6-sol, the model config.toml ALREADY pinned. Running the updated 0.147.0 client refreshed it to 8 and revealed gpt-5.6-sol (priority 1), gpt-5.6-terra (2), gpt-5.6-luna (3). Reading first yields a confidently wrong answer about what 'latest' even is. Pi ships this discipline as `pi update --models`.
_pin_proof_rule: 🚨 A CONFIG WRITE IS NOT A PIN. A --model/--reasoning flag passed through a wrapper can be silently ignored — no error, just quietly worse output — while the provider's own config file governs. A pin counts as PROVEN only when the agent was RUN and reported its own model id back (codex exec prints `model: gpt-5.6-sol` in its header and the agent echoes it). `proven_by` records how; a null there means UNPROVEN and renders as such.
